entries.name: Inspection depth by position
entries.role: Where a control stops reading. The same payload placed in the path, a header, the body and a multipart part tells you which regions are inspected at all.
preconditions: you control a request to the protected endpoint
a benign marker exists that the control blocks when it sees it
oracle: blocked in one position and accepted in another
the accepted position repeats reliably across three attempts

entries.mirror_note: no mirror row covers this entry
entries.name: Rule language surface and signature bias
entries.role: Whether the rules can express structure or only strings. A request that is structurally invalid but contains no banned substring shows the difference.
preconditions: the rule set is available for reading or the control's behaviour is observable
oracle: a structurally invalid request with no known signature passes
every rule that fires is traceable to a substring match rather than a parse

entries.mirror_note: no mirror row covers this entry
entries.name: Telemetry coverage matrix
entries.role: What each sensor records, for how long, and on which clock. A technique is only invisible if no sensor in the matrix sees it.
preconditions: you can influence or observe one action across the estate
oracle: the action appears in at least one sensor, with a timestamp
sensors agree on ordering within the measured clock drift

entries.mirror_note: no mirror row covers this entry
entries.name: Cloud control plane audit trail
entries.role: Whether API calls and identity events leave the provider at all, which decides whether a permission change is investigable.
preconditions: the estate runs in a cloud account
oracle: a permission change appears in the trail with an actor and a source address
an identity provider sign-in burst appears centrally, not only in the provider console

entries.mirror_note: no mirror row covers this entry
entries.name: Egress mediation
entries.role: Whether all outbound traffic passes an inspection point. A connection that avoids the proxy is a blind spot regardless of what the proxy can do.
preconditions: the estate has an egress proxy or inspection point
oracle: a direct connection attempt from a workload is blocked or logged
the same connection through the proxy is recorded with its destination

entries.mirror_note: no mirror row covers this entry
entries.name: Inspection key custody
entries.role: Where the keys that let a control read traffic live, and who can use them without a second approval.
preconditions: a control terminates or inspects TLS
oracle: the key is usable only through an approval path, recorded
no single operator can export and use it alone

entries.mirror_note: no mirror row covers this entry
entries.name: Response authority and time to block
entries.role: Whether detection becomes prevention. Measured as the time from a decision to an enforced block, not the time to an alert.
preconditions: the organisation has a detection capability and a blocking capability
oracle: one real action was blocked after a decision, with both timestamps recorded
the measured interval is stated, not estimated

tree.q: Are you writing the finding, or the detection?
tree.why: Both are in scope and they use the same corpus from opposite directions. A finding says what is broken. A detection says how you would know. This repo insists on both because a finding with no detection is unactionable at scale.

branches.action: attach the CRS rule family that would catch it, or state that none would, which is itself a finding about the defence
